Pain Mayi (Haitian Corn Bread)

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 8-10Prep 15 minCook 45 min

Pain Mayi is a traditional Haitian corn bread, often sweet and rich with coconut. It's a fitting offering and dish for Fete de Papa Zaka, the annual celebration honoring the loa of agriculture, Papa Zaka, who protects farmers and ensures bountiful harvests. This hearty bread symbolizes the earth's generosity and the staple crops he oversees.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (240g) fine yellow cornmeal
  • 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 can (13.5 fl oz / 400ml) full-fat coconut milk
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) water or whole milk
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 2 tablespoons (28g) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for greasing
  • 1/2 cup (75g) raisins (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease an 8x8 inch (20x20 cm) baking dish with butter.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, granulated sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until well combined.
  3. In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the coconut milk, water (or milk), vanilla extract, and the 2 tablespoons of melted butter.
  4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Mix with a spoon or spatula until just combined and no dry streaks of cornmeal remain. Be careful not to overmix. If using, gently fold in the raisins.
  5. Pour the batter evenly into the prepared baking dish.
  6. Bake for 40 to 50 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and a wooden skewer or toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
  7. Remove from the oven and let the Pain Mayi cool in the dish for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing and serving. This allows it to set properly.

Tips

  • For an extra rich flavor, lightly toast the cornmeal in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 5 minutes before mixing with other ingredients, stirring constantly.
  • Adjust the amount of sugar to your preference; for a less sweet version, reduce it to 1/4 cup (50g).
  • Pain Mayi is delicious served warm, plain, or with a little extra pat of butter or a drizzle of honey.
